section: Area Ratios Related to Side Length Ratios
subtopic: Area ratios and the angle bisector theorem
text: In the diagram below, angle $ABC$ is a right angle. Point $D$ is on $\overline{BC}$, and $\overline{AD}$ bisects angle $CAB$. Points $E$ and $F$ are on $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$, respectively, so that $AE = 3$ and $AF = 10$. Given that $EB = 9$ and $FC = 27$, find the integer closest to the area of quadrilateral $DCFG$.
figure: Right triangle ABC with the right angle at B (a right-angle mark is drawn at B): A is at the top left, B at the bottom left and C at the bottom right, so AB is vertical and BC is horizontal. E is on AB with AE labeled 3 and EB labeled 9. F is on AC with AF labeled 10 and FC labeled 27. D is on BC. Segment AD (the angle bisector of angle BAC) and segment EF are drawn; they cross at G, which lies on EF between E and F. The quadrilateral DCFG has vertices D, C, F, G. Segment EF looks nearly horizontal in the picture, but nothing says it is parallel to BC.
